title: Beyond Saxony-Anhalt: What Merz’s crisis means for Europe – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: The AfD's 43.8% in Saxony-Anhalt puts the far right within reach of Germany's first far-right state government and deepens splits inside Friedrich Merz's CDU/CSU, making him less able to deliver European leadership on the 2028-2034 EU budget or enlargement. ECFR's advice: other capitals should cut their expectations of Berlin and route ambition through the E6 and the Ukraine “coalition of the willing”.

insights.claim: The AfD took 43.8% in Saxony-Anhalt and 39 of the seats — three short of a majority — leaving it needing the left-conservative BSW or the CDU's right flank to form what would be the first far-right state government in the history of the German federal republic.
insights.so_what: A concrete coalition-arithmetic trigger: whether the CDU's right flank breaks the firewall is the single event to watch for German political risk repricing.
insights.locator: Saxony-Anhalt has returned 43.8% of the vote
insights.speaker: Jeremy Cliffe, Jana Puglierin

insights.claim: The consequences of an AfD-led state government are binary: chaotic governance would deter voters elsewhere from backing such parties, while halfway coherent governance would give it leeway to pilot policies and embolden the radical right across Europe.
insights.so_what: Gives a clean two-branch scenario tree for Europe-wide far-right contagion over the next two years.
insights.locator: The AfD has no executive experience
insights.speaker: Jeremy Cliffe, Jana Puglierin

insights.claim: Saxony-Anhalt is demographically unrepresentative — an atypically old and homogeneous population of 2.1m against a German total of 83.5m — yet the result has still reverberated through European capitals.
insights.so_what: Cautions against extrapolating the vote share nationally while acknowledging the signalling effect is real.
insights.locator: Saxony-Anhalt is a small and demographically unrepresentative German state
insights.speaker: Jeremy Cliffe, Jana Puglierin

themes.theme: Merz's weakening and the European leadership vacuum

insights.claim: Merz is now even less likely to achieve a breakthrough on the EU's 2028-2034 budget negotiations or on EU accession talks, so other leaders including Ursula von der Leyen will need to depend less on him to advance ambitious proposals.
insights.so_what: Directly lowers the probability of an ambitious MFF deal and of enlargement progress on the current timetable — relevant to anyone pricing EU fiscal capacity or Western Balkans/Ukraine accession.
insights.quote: Merz, for example, is now even less likely to achieve a breakthrough on the EU’s 2028-2034 budget negotiations or on EU accession talks.
insights.locator: Other European capitals should curb their expectations
insights.speaker: Jeremy Cliffe, Jana Puglierin

insights.claim: Splits inside the CDU/CSU between eastern and western branches, and between Merz and his conservative base, were already widening before the vote and are now worse, raising the chance he is too distracted by domestic politics to lead in Europe.
insights.so_what: German domestic fragmentation, not European institutional design, is the binding constraint on EU decision-making in this cycle.
insights.locator: Meanwhile the result increases the pressure
insights.speaker: Jeremy Cliffe, Jana Puglierin

insights.claim: With France, Italy, Poland and Spain all entering election seasons simultaneously, a Germany consumed by internal drama cannot be the anchor Europe needs.
insights.so_what: A rare window in which every major EU state is politically constrained at once — expect drift and minimal new EU-level commitments through the election cycle.
insights.quote: With France, Italy, Poland and Spain all entering election seasons, a Germany riven by internal drama cannot be the anchor that Europe needs.
insights.locator: With France, Italy, Poland and Spain all entering election seasons
insights.speaker: Jeremy Cliffe, Jana Puglierin

insights.claim: Two further state elections on September 20th in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin could dent Merz's authority further, and while not currently probable, it is possible he is forced out as chancellor in the coming months, with North Rhine-Westphalia premier Hendrik Wüst the obvious frontrunner.
insights.so_what: A dated, checkable catalyst for German leadership risk, with a named successor whose moderate politics may not fit the polarised mood.
insights.locator: Two upcoming state elections on September 20th
insights.speaker: Jeremy Cliffe, Jana Puglierin

insights.claim: Merz's fragile grand coalition is already struggling to pass the reforms aimed at reviving Germany's stagnant economy, and the election result compounds that paralysis.
insights.so_what: Links political fragility directly to the reform agenda underpinning any German growth recovery thesis.
insights.locator: The development comes as Merz’s fragile “grand coalition”
insights.speaker: Jeremy Cliffe, Jana Puglierin

themes.theme: Prescriptions: bans, funding streams and alternative coalitions

insights.claim: Talk of banning the AfD is too late and would not quell underlying voter discontent; action against stand-out extremists and the party's funding streams is more realistic and more likely to keep its voters persuadable.
insights.so_what: Sets a testable policy path — watch for federal moves against AfD financing rather than a party-ban process.
insights.locator: Bold action is needed both in Berlin and beyond Germany
insights.speaker: Jeremy Cliffe, Jana Puglierin

insights.claim: European capitals should nurture broader sources of impetus, including the new E6 group of major EU economies and the “coalition of the willing” on Ukraine, rather than waiting on Berlin.
insights.so_what: Identifies where European decisions will actually be made in the near term: coalitions of the willing and the E6, not the European Council.
insights.locator: Other European capitals should curb their expectations
insights.speaker: Jeremy Cliffe, Jana Puglierin
